messages:
meera: Quick follow-up from today's RFC sync — small proposal: add a 'migration_score' field to rollout metadata to help runtime decide when to softly evict a sticky ref and prefer a newer variant. Keeping this thread short, want quick ok/nok and edge cases.

jordan: +1 on surfacing a numeric signal. can we define range and semantics? integer 0-100? higher => more willing to migrate?

samir: I like numeric. Suggest: migration_score [0..100], higher means more eligible to be rolled forward. Also add 'stability_score' [0..100] that represents observed quality regressions. runtime picks variant with highest (migration_score - stability_penalty).

ophelia: Concern: clients might rely on sticky refs for long-lived sessions. We should keep a soft TTL and an explicit client-probe option. propose field: soft_ttl_seconds. default 3600 (1h).

meera: Great points. Draft metadata example:
```json
{
  "variant_id": "model-x-v2.3",
  "migration_score": 60,
  "stability_score": 85,
  "canary_pct": 10,
  "soft_ttl_seconds": 3600,
  "grace_window_ms": 30000,
  "fallback_policy": ["pinned_alias","nearest_compat"],
  "telemetry_tags": ["user-facing","high-cost"]
}
```

jordan: +1 for explicit soft_ttl. what is grace_window_ms?

meera: grace_window_ms: how long the runtime will accept overlapped probes during a rollforward before forcing strict selection. handles clock skew and queued requests. default 30s.

samir: Implementation note: runtime should compute "migration_priority = migration_score - (100 - stability_score)". That gives stable new variants a boost; unstable ones get penalized. Also tie-breaker by canary_pct and last_updated_ts.

ophelia: Ops question: how do we surface this in Console? want a short human label and link to recent eval sets. propose adding 'reason_short' and 'eval_link' as optional strings in metadata.

meera: Agree. Add optional fields: reason_short and eval_ref. Also ops will need rollout-level flags to disable auto-evict for enterprise tenants, so add "auto_evict": true/false.

infra-bot: Note: autoscaler applied to pool-2 at 1768510100, no impact to variant routing. :white_check_mark:

jordan: Edge case: downstream clients with pinned session tokens — we should allow a client header `Prefer-Stable: true|false`. If true, server will consider only variants with stability_score >= 80.

samir: Good call. Also recommend exposing a compact encoding for mobile clients: `compact_hint=ms:60,ss:85,ttl:3600` to keep header size tiny.

ophelia: For rollout migration windows, propose a backoff schedule on eviction attempts: 0s, 30s, 2m, 10m, 1h — tied to grace_window_ms multiplier. Logs should include eviction_attempt_id so SRE can trace.

meera: Action items: 1) update rollout metadata schema with fields discussed (migration_score, stability_score, soft_ttl_seconds, grace_window_ms, auto_evict, reason_short, eval_ref). 2) add runtime scoring formula to the rollout RFC appendix. 3) add Console UI field for eval_ref + human reason. 4) add client header docs for Prefer-Stable and compact_hint.

jordan: I'm fine with defaults: migration_score=50, stability_score=100 for existing variants, soft_ttl_seconds=3600, grace_window_ms=30000, auto_evict=true.

ophelia: I'll follow up with a short ops playbook for how to override auto_evict for enterprise tenants and how to interpret migration_priority in incidents.

meera: Thanks all. If no strong objections by EOD I'll fold this into the RFC as a follow-up appendix. :thumbsup:
